cards.text: Hosea, a prophet in Israel (Hosea 1:1), is still bringing the word of the LORD, and the LORD has a case against the people of the land (Hosea 4:1). Now the LORD calls out three groups by name. First up: "Hear this, O priests!"

cards.question: The LORD calls out the priests first. Who else does He name in this judgment?

answers.text: The house of Israel and the royal house
The prophets and the elders of the land
The soldiers and the judges at the gate

cards.text: That's the boss leaning out of the office going, "EVERYBODY. In here. NOW." Then the LORD names two places, Mizpah and Tabor, and says what they've been there.

cards.question: The LORD says this judgment is against them because they have been a ___ at Mizpah, a net spread out on Tabor.

cards.text: The ones who should lead people home set the trap. That's your GPS cheerfully saying, "Turn right," and right is the LAKE. Then the LORD says the rebels are deep in slaughter.

cards.question: The rebels are deep in slaughter. True or false: the LORD says He will chastise only the worst of them.

cards.text: Ephraim, one of Israel's tribes, gets named right alongside Israel here. The LORD says, "I know all about Ephraim, and Israel is not hidden from Me."

cards.question: The LORD sees it all. He says Ephraim has turned to ___, and Israel is defiled.

cards.text: And here's the heavy part. The LORD says their deeds don't let them return to their God.

cards.question: Israel's deeds keep them from returning to God. What does the LORD say is inside them?
Israel has a spirit of prostitution inside them. True or false: the LORD says they still know Him.

cards.text: Then the LORD says Israel's arrogance testifies against them. Their own pride takes the witness stand, and friend, it is TALKING.

cards.question: Israel and Ephraim stumble in their iniquity. True or false: Judah, the kingdom to the south, stays on its feet.

cards.text: So they set out to seek the LORD, bringing their flocks and herds with them. That's not a visit, friend, that's a moving truck with HOOVES.

cards.question: Israel shows up with their flocks and herds to seek the LORD. What happens?
Israel seeks the LORD and doesn't find Him. What does the text say He has done?

answers.text: He has withdrawn Himself from them
He has sent them to the prophets
He has gone to Judah instead

cards.text: The LORD says they've been unfaithful to Him, and they have borne illegitimate children. Then He names what's coming: the New Moon will devour them.

cards.question: The New Moon will devour the people. True or false: the LORD says it will devour their land too.

cards.text: Then the alarm goes up: blow the ram's horn in Gibeah and the trumpet in Ramah. A horn AND a trumpet, friend, that's the smoke alarm at 3 a.m. while you're up on a chair waving a dish towel at it.

cards.question: The horns blow in Gibeah and Ramah. What goes up in Beth-aven?

cards.text: Then the LORD speaks about the day of rebuke for Ephraim. And He's not guessing: among the tribes of Israel, He proclaims what is certain.

cards.question: True or false: on the day of rebuke, Ephraim will be laid waste.

cards.text: Judah's leaders don't get a pass. The LORD says the princes of Judah are like those who move boundary stones, like the neighbor who scoots the fence over a foot every summer and hopes you won't notice.

cards.question: About the princes of Judah, the LORD says He will pour out His fury upon them like ___.

cards.text: Back to Ephraim. He's oppressed, crushed in judgment.

cards.question: Ephraim is crushed in judgment. Why?

answers.text: He is determined to follow worthless idols
He refused to pay tribute to Judah
He broke a treaty he made with Egypt

cards.text: Now the LORD picks a picture for what He is to Ephraim and to Judah.

cards.question: The LORD says He is like a ___ to Ephraim, and like decay to the house of Judah.

cards.text: A moth. You don't hear it, you don't see it, and then you pull out your favorite sweater and it's a FISHING NET. Then Ephraim sees his sickness, and Judah sees his wound.

cards.question: Ephraim finally sees how sick he is. Where does he turn for help?
Ephraim sends to the great king of Assyria. True or false: the great king can cure Ephraim and heal the wound.

cards.text: That's like breaking your arm and asking the group chat to set it. Then the LORD says He is like a lion to Ephraim, and like a young lion to the house of Judah.

cards.question: The LORD is like a lion to Ephraim. What does He say He will do?

answers.text: Tear them to pieces and go away
Guard them all through the night
Chase off every one of their enemies

cards.question: The LORD says He will carry them off. True or false: someone will be able to rescue them.

cards.text: The LORD has been talking like a lion. Now He says He'll return to His place and wait.

cards.question: The LORD says He'll stay in His place until they admit their ___ and seek His ___.

cards.text: He says that in their affliction, they will earnestly seek Him. Then the voice changes, and a call goes out: "Come, let us return to the LORD."

cards.question: The call admits the LORD has torn them to pieces and wounded them. What does it say He will do?

answers.text: Heal us and bind up our wounds
Give us a new king to follow
Choose a new people for Himself

cards.text: Torn up, then bound up. I'm a worn-down stamper who got made new, so friend, that line hits me RIGHT in the apron.

cards.question: The call says that after two days He will revive us. True or false: it says on the third day He will raise us up.

cards.text: So the call puts it plain: let us press on to know the LORD. PRESS ON, friend, not hit snooze nine times and roll over.

cards.question: The call says, "As surely as the sun rises, He will appear." What does that picture say about the LORD's coming?

answers.text: It will only happen in the morning
It will happen just one time

cards.question: The call says He will come to us like the ___, like the spring showers that water the earth.
